thread:
maya: Quick check — I ran a multi-region p50/p95 sweep for the new llama3-small int8 build across H100/A100 in us-east / us-west / eu-west. High-level: routing to nearest edge helped p50 but eu-west p95 spiked when traffic hit the proxy-pop. Results + notes below.

ravi: Can you paste the raw numbers and kernel variants?

maya: Short summary:
- h100 (us-east): p50=48ms, p95=120ms
- a100 (us-east): p50=60ms, p95=140ms
- h100 (us-west, edge-direct): p50=52ms, p95=130ms
- h100 (eu-west, routed via proxy-pop): p50=70ms, p95=180ms
Quant: int8 (aware quantizer), kernel: fused-attn v2 primary, fallback to cuBLAS for seq>2048.

sam: Any quality regressions from int8?

maya: Minor — eval harness shows avg ~0.6 BLEU drop on our paraphrase set, but some outliers on arithmetic prompts. Not catastrophic but worth tracking.

lin: Did you compare routing policies (prefer-region vs prefer-lowest-latency)?

maya: Yes. prefer-lowest-latency lowers p50 globally (10-15ms) but increases p95 in eu-west due to a proxy-pop failover pattern. prefer-region yields steadier tails but slightly higher median. Repro steps:

```
# bench command used
python bench/run.py --model llama3-small --quant int8 --nodes h100,a100 \
  --regions us-east us-west eu-west \
  --routing prefer-lowest-latency --trials 300 --seq_len 1024
```

maya: Perf artifact: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/bench/1732105555/summary.csv (uploaded by ci-bot)

ci-bot: perf-bench: New artifact uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/bench/1732105555/summary.csv

ravi: Can you attach the eu-west latency histogram and any proxy logs around the spike window? Need to see if it's network jitter or kernel GC.

maya: Pulled snippet: eu-west p95 spike lines up with proxy-pop failover at ~t=15m (we see ~300ms retransmit window). Kernel-level logs show repeated fallback to cuBLAS for a handful of long sequences during the same interval.

sam: Hypothesis: routing oscillation causes a small fanout -> transient queueing at proxy-pop -> longer tails. Combined with kernel fallback for long seqs, that pushes p95 up. Two mitigations: pin routing for eu-west to prefer-region for canary, and set threshold to avoid kernel fallback churn.

lin: Also check KV-cache warmup — small bursty traffic shows higher p95 because cache miss rate is correlated with route changes. Did bench include warmup runs?

maya: Yes, bench did 50 warmup queries per client but not a sustained soak. Next steps I propose: 1) run 24h soak with prefer-region in eu-west; 2) try int4 on H100-only to measure latency/quality tradeoff; 3) add tracing spans to edge-proxy to capture failover stack traces; 4) fine-tune kernel fallback threshold to seq>1024 instead of 2048.

ravi: +1 to soak and add edge trace. If soak shows stable tails, we can enable prefer-region for eu-west traffic tiered by customer.

sam: Also recommend adding a p95 alert specifically for region-proxy failovers so ops gets realtime nudges.

maya: Will schedule the soak and post results here. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary routing policy change applied to eu-west pref-region for test group at 2024-04-12T18:02:31Z

lin: One more ask — can you attach the raw CSV percentiles besides the summary? I want 50/75/90/95/99 buckets for the soak.

maya: Uploading full CSV to artifact store now, will link when done.

maya: follow-up: uploaded full csv and histograms: https://ci.redwood.ai/artifacts/bench/1732105555/full_report.zip

ravi: Thanks — I’ll look at packet-level traces if p95 persists after soak.

maya: Noted. Will run int4 test on H100 tomorrow and post delta.

sam: Great. If int4 quality is acceptable, that could shrink p50 and p95 across H100 by ~8-12ms from reduced kernel time.

maya: Closing note: prefer-lowest-latency is attractive for medians, but for eu-west we should prioritize tail stability until proxy-pop failover behavior is hardened.

lin: Agreed.

maya: End of thread.
